content: 1. Nitroglycerin-induced reflex tachycardia can be mitigated by beta-blockers without interfering with its blood pressure-lowering effects. However, when beta-blockers are used in combination with nitroglycerin in patients with angina pectoris, additional hypotensive effects may occur. 2. The concurrent use of nitroglycerin rectal and lisinopril may enhance the effects of each other due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Caution is advised, and monitoring for additive hypotensive effects is recommended. 3.
